title: Presheaf point pullback on affine objects
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\mathbf{Prof}$ have compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces as objects and continuous maps as arrows, with finite jointly surjective coverings. For $S\in\mathbf{Prof}$, let $X[S]$ be the inverse limit over the finite continuous quotients $S\to S_i$ of the finite disjoint unions $\coprod_{S_i}X$, and let $a_X(S)=X[S]$. For a sheaf $F$ of sets, abelian groups, or commutative rings on $\mathbf{Prof}$, let $P_F$ be the presheaf left Kan extension of its underlying presheaf along $a_X^{op}$, so $P_F(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{(U\to X[S])}F(S)$, with transitions induced by precomposition on $F$. Let $U$ be a weakly contractible affine object of the pro-etale site, meaning every epimorphism of sheaves of sets is surjective on sections over $U$. Then the quotient space $\pi_0(|U|)$ of connected components, with quotient topology, is profinite, and there is a canonical isomorphism $P_F(U)\cong F(\pi_0(|U|))$, natural in $F$ and in weakly contractible affine $U$. In particular, for every finite family of weakly contractible affine objects $U_i$, the restriction map $P_F(\coprod_iU_i)\to\prod_iP_F(U_i)$ is an isomorphism, including the empty family. The isomorphisms preserve the indicated algebraic operations.

proof.text: For the weakly contractible affine object $U$, the quotient $\pi_0(|U|)$ is profinite and maps from $U$ to every finite-quotient object $X[S]$ are exactly continuous maps $\pi_0(|U|)\to S$, compatibly with refinement and with morphisms of affine objects, by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-point-components-maps].

source.place: Lemma 4.2.13(1), first sentence of proof; exact master RefactorInstruction.tex, Section 4, proof of Lemma point-pullback formula.

proof.text: Put $T=\pi_0(|U|)$ and let $q:U\to X[T]$ correspond to $\mathrm{id}_T$ in step 1. The Kan index has objects $(S,f:U\to X[S])$ and a morphism $(S,f)\to(S\prime,f\prime)$ is a continuous map $h:S\prime\to S$ with $f=X[h]\circ f\prime$; its diagram map is $F(h):F(S)\to F(S\prime)$. By step 1, $f$ corresponds to a unique $g:T\to S$, so $g$ gives the unique arrow $(S,f)\to(T,q)$. Thus $(T,q)$ is terminal. Explicitly the colimit cocone is $F(g):F(S)\to F(T)$: for a compatible cocone $c_{S,f}:F(S)\to A$, compatibility with the unique terminal arrow forces $c_{S,f}=c_{T,q}\circ F(g)$. Conversely any map $F(T)\to A$ defines this cocone. This proves the colimit universal property in sets, abelian groups and rings, giving $P_F(U)\cong F(T)$ without asserting continuity through finite-quotient colimits.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-point-lan-affine-evaluation-finite-products] for the finite coproduct restriction cone. For the evaluation isomorphism, choose the inverse of the Kan cocone leg at the terminal object constructed in step 2. The cocone naturality equation gives its normalization on every leg. To prove simultaneous naturality in the affine object and the coefficient sheaf, use pointwise Kan cocone hom_ext, the unit compatibility, and the two naturalities from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-point-components-maps]. Functoriality and naturality of the coefficient morphism identify the resulting composites. This argument works in any coefficient category; specialize to types, abelian groups and commutative rings, so all maps preserve the corresponding operations.
